record.original_question: Do there exist normed spaces D and E for which the H_2 norm of a linear-system transfer function is an induced operator norm? The source asks whether one can realize the H_2 performance measure as a true induced norm between suitable signal spaces rather than only as an energy-like quantity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G(s)$ be a strictly proper, stable rational matrix-valued transfer function on the open right half-plane, viewed as an element of the Hardy space $H_2$ with norm
$$\|G\|_{H_2} := \left(\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \operatorname{tr}\bigl(G(j\omega)^* G(j\omega)\bigr)\,d\omega\right)^{1/2}.$$
Equivalently, if $G$ is the transfer function of a linear time-invariant input/output operator $\mathcal{G}:u\mapsto y$, the $H_2$ norm coincides with the $L_2$ norm of the impulse response.

Question: Do there exist normed signal spaces $(D,\|\cdot\|_D)$ and $(E,\|\cdot\|_E)$, together with a realization of $\mathcal{G}$ as a bounded linear operator $\mathcal{G}:D\to E$, such that
$$\|G\|_{H_2} \;=\; \|\mathcal{G}\|_{D\to E} \;:=\; \sup_{u\in D,\;u\neq 0}\frac{\|\mathcal{G}u\|_E}{\|u\|_D}\,?$$
That is, can the $H_2$ performance measure be expressed as a genuine induced (operator) norm of $\mathcal{G}$ between suitable normed spaces of input and output signals?
artifact.category_tag: H2 norm and induced operator norms in control
artifact.status_search_result: Standard references state that the $H_\infty$ norm of an LTI system is an induced ($L_2\to L_2$) norm, whereas the $H_2$ norm is usually described only as an "energy" or stochastic measure and not as an induced norm in the classical sense. A targeted web search did not turn up a published result either constructing such normed spaces $D,E$ that induce the $H_2$ norm or proving that no such pair exists, so the status of this specific question is unclear from available sources.

status_evidence.title: Interpretation of H2 and H-Infinity Norms - MathWorks
status_evidence.snippet: H-infinity norm equals the induced L2 norm of the system; H2 norm is described via white-noise/energy interpretations, not as an induced norm.
status_evidence.claim: The H-infinity norm is presented as an induced norm while the H2 norm is presented via energy/variance interpretations.

status_evidence.title: Signal and system norms
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses signal/system norms including H2 and H-infinity; H-infinity is the L2-induced norm.
status_evidence.claim: Standard treatment does not present the H2 norm as an induced operator norm between signal spaces.
